# @zakkster/lite-i18n

> Zero-GC reactive internationalization built on @zakkster/lite-signal. Compile
> messages once at defineMessages -- runtime lookup is one Map.get and one fn
> call, allocating nothing but the returned string. Synchronous reactive flush,
> no microtask scheduler. ESM-only, ~3.5 KB min+gz core + ~0.76 KB Format entry,
> single peer dep on @zakkster/lite-signal (^1.4.0), MIT licensed.

The library exposes translation primitives (t, plural, locale, defineMessages),
async loading (loadLocale, ready), fallback chain, missing-key policies, and a
tree-shakeable Intl formatter surface (number, date, list, relative-time) with
both convenience and factory forms. Built for animation loops, Twitch
Extensions, game HUDs, per-tenant SDKs, and SSR (one instance per request).

## Core concepts

- **Message**: a template string. Three internal shapes: static (`"Welcome"`),
  interpolation (`"Hi, {name}"`), or inline plural (`"{count, plural, one
  {# item} other {# items}}"`). Compiled at defineMessages into a closure over
  a stable token array.

- **Dict**: a namespace. Values are strings, plural-object entries
  (`{ one, other, =0, ... }`), or nested dicts. Nested dicts flatten to
  dot-paths at define time so runtime lookup is a single Map.get.

- **Plural-object entry**: an object with an `other` key and only CLDR
  selectors (`zero`, `one`, `two`, `few`, `many`, `other`) or exact patterns
  (`=0`, `=1`, ...) as own-property keys. Detected structurally at define
  time. Missing `other` -> treated as nested dict.

- **Inline arguments**: three ICU-lite constructs, all balanced-brace,
  freely nested inside each other's sub-templates.
  - `{var, plural, sel {sub} ...}` -- cardinal plural via
    `Intl.PluralRules`.
  - `{var, selectordinal, sel {sub} ...}` (v1.1) -- ordinal plural via
    `Intl.PluralRules(loc, { type: "ordinal" })`. Same selector alphabet
    as plural (`one two few many other`, `=N`).
  - `{var, select, sel {sub} ...}` (v1.1) -- string-keyed dispatch, no
    `Intl.PluralRules` call. Selectors are bare identifiers, `other`
    required.
  `#` inside plural/selectordinal sub-templates is shorthand for `{var}`.
  Nested plural/select/selectordinal inside any sub-template is supported;
  unsupported ICU shapes (`{n, number}`, `{d, date, short}`,
  `{n, number, ::currency/EUR}`, `{n, choice, ...}`) throw `SyntaxError`
  at define time -- same guard, whether at top level or nested.

- **Reactive signals**: each instance holds a `_locale` signal (current
  locale) and a `_epoch` signal (bumped on defineMessages for active/fallback
  locales, and on setFallback). `t()` and `plural()` subscribe to both, so
  effects/computeds re-run on any change.

- **Fallback chain**: array of locales walked in order when a key is missing
  in the current locale. The active locale is skipped if listed. Chain flips
  bump the epoch. Defining messages for a locale NOT in `[active, ...chain]`
  does NOT bump the epoch (avoids spurious re-fires for lazy chunks belonging
  to other locales).

- **Missing-key policy**: `"key"` (default -- return literal), `"warn"`
  (console.warn + return literal), `"throw"` (throw `MissingKeyError`).
  Fallback chain walks BEFORE the policy fires. Optional `onMissingKey(key,
  locale)` hook can short-circuit; return a string to use it, return void to
  fall through.

- **Async loader**: `loadLocale(loc, fn)` runs a user-supplied loader, caches
  the dict, and flips `ready(loc)` signal to true. Race-safe: in-flight calls
  share a promise; already-loaded resolves immediately without calling the
  loader; errors clear the in-flight slot so callers can retry.

- **Isolated instance**: `createI18n(config)` creates a fresh reactive world
  with its own signals, dicts, and PluralRules cache. Multiple instances
  share nothing. `setDefaultI18n(inst)` swaps the instance used by top-level
  helpers; `locale` is an ESM live binding so importers see the new signal
  on next reference (destructured captures are stale).

- **Formatters** (`@zakkster/lite-i18n/format`): reactive wrappers around
  `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `Intl.ListFormat`,
  `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`. Two shapes: convenience (`formatNumber(v, opts,
  i18n?)`) with WeakMap(opts)-keyed cache; factory (`numberFormat(opts,
  i18n?)`) returning a per-locale-cached `(value) => string`. Convenience is
  zero-alloc for hoisted opts; factory is zero-alloc unconditionally after
  the first call per locale.

## Architecture invariants

- **Compile once, reuse forever**: `defineMessages` walks the dict, flattens
  nested paths, tokenizes each template, and compiles a closure per entry.
  The closure signature is `(params, locale, getPluralRules) => string`.
  Compiled entries stored in `Map<locale, Map<key, fn>>`.

- **Uniform call site**: every compiled entry -- static, simple, plural-obj,
  inline-plural -- has the same signature. Monomorphic invocation at the
  lookup site is critical for V8 IC performance.

- **Token types**: 0 = literal (`{ str }`), 1 = slot (`{ key }`), 2 = plural
  block (`{ variable, exact: Map<number, tokens>, variants: Map<selector,
  tokens> }`). Sub-templates inside plural variants use only types 0 and 1;
  `#` compiles to `{ type: 1, key: <plural variable> }`.

- **PluralRules cache**: `Map<locale, Intl.PluralRules>` per instance. Lazy;
  one instance per unique locale used with a plural. Bounded at
  `LOCALE_CACHE_MAX` (256) and FIFO-evicted -- entries are pure `(locale, type)`
  memos, so reconstructing an evicted one renders byte-identically. FIFO, not
  LRU, because LRU would require recency bookkeeping on the cache HIT (the hot
  path); the eviction only runs in the cache-MISS branch that already builds an
  ICU object.

- **Readiness-signal cache**: `Map<locale, Signal<boolean>>` per instance. A
  signal carries subscriber IDENTITY, so it is NEVER silently evicted -- it fails
  CLOSED at `LOCALE_CACHE_MAX` with a named `LocaleCapacityError`. Feed `ready()`
  bounded input via `resolveLocale`, never raw untrusted locale strings.

- **32-bit modular epoch**: `_epoch` is bumped via `(n + 1) | 0`, wrapping
  signed. lite-signal handles the modular comparison; the counter never
  overflows.

- **String allocation is the only per-call allocation**: the token loop
  builds the result via `out += ...`. No intermediate arrays or objects. No
  regex per call.

- **Reactivity is synchronous**: `_epoch.set(v)` -> `t()` calls in dependent
  effects flush in the same call stack. Same discipline as lite-signal.

## Performance characteristics

- `t()` with static template -- O(1), zero alloc (except the returned string).
- `t()` with N slots -- O(N), zero alloc.
- `t()` with inline plural -- O(N + P) where P is size of the winning variant.
- `plural(key, count, params?)` -- one small merge alloc for `{...params,
  count}`. For hot loops, use `t(key, params)` with `count` in `params`.
- `formatNumber(v, opts)` (hoisted opts) -- one Map.get + Intl format call.
- `numberFormat(opts)()` (factory) -- one Map.get + Intl format call. Same,
  no WeakMap layer.
- `defineMessages` -- O(entries * template length). Allocation-heavy; not on
  hot path.
- `setFallback` / `defineMessages` for active or fallback locale -- bump
  epoch, O(observers). Standard signal cost.
- `loadLocale` -- O(1) + Promise infrastructure (unavoidable). Not for hot
  paths.

## Version notes

- **1.2.0** (2026-08-16, bounded caches + eviction). Every per-locale structure
  was unbounded and nothing released one; the three fail in OPPOSITE directions,
  so they take DIFFERENT policies (decisions/0003-locale-bounds.md). I-03:
  `ready()` cached one lite-signal per distinct locale string and at ~1020 tags
  exhausted lite-signal's process-wide 1024-node pool, poisoning every lite-*
  package in the process. Now `ready()` fails CLOSED at `LOCALE_CACHE_MAX` (256)
  with a NAMED `LocaleCapacityError` (per-instance blast radius, not lite-signal's
  process-wide `CapacityError`) -- a signal carries subscriber identity, so it is
  never silently evicted. I-04: `_pluralRules` / `_ordinalRules` grew unbounded
  keyed on the raw (untrusted) locale when a fallback chain was configured (3000
  distinct locales -> 3000 cached ICU objects; WITHOUT a fallback the key misses
  first and 0 are cached). Now FIFO-evicted at `LOCALE_CACHE_MAX` with NO throw --
  these are pure `(locale, type)` memos, so reconstructing an evicted entry is
  byte-identical (proven by the eviction-equivalence torture test). Eviction is
  FIFO, not LRU, because LRU needs recency bookkeeping on every cache HIT, which is
  the hot path. I-19: warn-once-per-tag was a log-flood surface reachable through
  `Accept-Language`; a per-instance `WARN_BUDGET` (32) now caps the warnings and
  counts the rest (`stats().warningsSuppressed`). I-12: `unloadLocale(loc)` drops
  the dict, both rules memos and the ready signal (removed from the map, THEN set
  false, so a subscriber still holding the reference sees the transition while a
  re-entrant `ready()` fired from inside that notification re-mints a fresh
  signal); `clear()` resets the instance to empty. `resolveLocale(
  requested, supported)` (BCP 47 prefix matching, no RFC 4647 tables) is the fix
  AT THE CALL SITE -- it bounds the untrusted stream to the app's own list.
  `stats()` gains `readySignalsCached`, `retiredLocales`, `warningsSuppressed`.
  `t()` and `plural()` take ZERO new instructions (bounds live in the cache-miss
  branch and in `ready()`, none of which is hot); I0's six Q2 ceilings are
  unmoved. The lite-leak retention witness stays deferred (I-14: `@zakkster/
  lite-leak` still peer-requires `lite-signal >=1.5.0-beta.3`; installed 1.4.0,
  registry latest 1.4.3 -- unresolvable).

- **1.1.4** (2026-08-15, security fix). I-01: prototype pollution could choose
  which variant rendered. The type-1 slot was `Object.hasOwn`-guarded, but the
  three selector reads were bare `params[key]` -- the `{var, plural, ...}` /
  `{var, selectordinal, ...}` variable and the `{var, select, ...}` variable
  (both in `renderTokens`), and the plural-object `count` (in
  `compilePluralObj`). A single
  `Object.prototype.gender = "male"` flipped `"They"` to `"He"`; `.count = 1`
  flipped `" items"` to `" item"` (with no number, since `#` is a guarded slot).
  Shipped in 1.1.2 and 1.1.3. Fixed with one `Object.hasOwn` per selector read
  (the same branch a slot already pays); an absent selector resolves to `other`,
  unchanged from before. I-02: the two prototype-pollution tests that stayed
  green over the bug now exercise every read site (`test/08-torture.test.mjs`)
  and the full identity matrix lands in `test/torture/t2-identity.mjs`. I-16:
  `VERSION` is now declared in `I18n.d.ts` and a version-sync test
  (`test/10-version-sync.test.mjs`) keeps the `.d.ts` in the sync set. I-17: the
  published `MessageParams` type drops `bigint` -- a bigint renders in a slot but
  throws out of `Intl.PluralRules.select`, so the declaration was narrowed rather
  than coercing at the selector (decisions/0002-selector-reads.md). Q2 allocation
  ceilings unmoved (`select` stayed at 0 scavenges/1M; the guard reads an own
  property and allocates nothing).

- **1.1.3** (2026-08-15, instrumentation). Added a `VERSION` export (three-place
  version sync: package.json / VERSION const / this file). Stood up the
  `test/torture.mjs` suite (10 tiers; `npm run torture`) and a size gate
  (`npm run size`). No behaviour change to the read/compile paths. The
  allocation gate settled which instrument answers which question
  (decisions/0001-measurement.md): Q1 retention via `measureAllocs`
  (maxBytesPerCall:0), Q2 transient via minor-GC (scavenge) count per 1M ops
  under a pinned new-space (torture.mjs re-execs with min==max semi-space for
  bit-identical, position-independent counts) -- committed per-shape ceilings
  and the `plural()` calibration number -- and Q3 pause via `checkNoGc`
  (maxMajor:0, maxPauseMs:4). Known
  issues recorded but NOT fixed this release: I-01 (prototype pollution can
  select a plural/select variant), I-03 (`ready()` exhausts the lite-signal
  node pool at ~1018 distinct locales), I-05 (`loadLocale` overwrites a later
  `defineMessages`); the lite-leak retention tier is deferred (I-14: no stable
  lite-signal >=1.5.0 to satisfy lite-leak's peer), and the call-site
  monomorphism law is an open question (a throughput ratio cannot witness it).

- **1.1.1** (2026-07-19, review fixes). Fixed `plural(key, count, params)`
  silently returning wrong strings on inline templates whose plural
  variable wasn't `count` (e.g. `{n, plural, ...}`) -- compiler now tags
  each compiled entry with `.pluralVar` scanned from top-level tokens,
  and `plural()` merges under that name. Added a define-time
  `console.warn` when a dict value is neither string nor plain object
  (numbers, arrays, null, undefined, etc.) so typos no longer lose keys
  silently. Extended the plural selector accumulator to letters + digits
  + underscore after the first letter so `many2` reaches the helpful
  "Unknown plural selector" error instead of "Expected '{' after
  selector". Guarded the Format entry against environments missing
  `Intl.ListFormat` / `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` (first-use error names
  the missing constructor and suggests a polyfill). Documented the
  all-string-CLDR-shaped-namespace ambiguity and the literal-dotted vs
  nested-path collision. Added `.gitignore`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
  (Node 18/20/22 matrix), and aligned `package.json` with the ecosystem
  convention (email in author + bugs, funding field, devDependencies
  mirroring peer). 175 behavior tests + 7 stress tests, 0 fail.
  Size: 3.5 KB min+gz core (+~200 B for pluralVar tagging and the
  selector fix), 0.76 KB Format (+~180 B for the guarded caches).

- **1.1.0** (2026-07-19). Added `select` (string-keyed dispatch, no
  PluralRules; token type 3) and `selectordinal` (ordinal categories via
  `Intl.PluralRules(loc, { type: "ordinal" })`; separate `_ordinalRules`
  cache; reported in `stats().ordinalRulesCached`). Both tokenizers route
  through a shared `parseArgument` so plural/select/selectordinal compose
  freely inside each other -- the canonical multi-axis ICU pattern is
  supported. Non-breaking: every v1.0.0 template still compiles to the
  same output. 163 behavior tests + 4 skipped GC in the default run
  (167 total); 7 stress tests under `--expose-gc` push to 1M-iteration
  workloads for simple/plural/select and 500k for composition. New
  torture suite (`test/08-torture.test.mjs`) covers unicode edges,
  regex-eating templates, parser corners, numeric edges, prototype
  pollution, reactive reentrancy, and three-axis composition. Size:
  3.3 KB min+gz core (v1.0.0 was 3.1 KB), Format entry unchanged.
  Bench harness in `bench/` compares against i18next and
  intl-messageformat -- lite-i18n leads all four workloads (3-6x vs
  formatjs, 12-56x vs i18next on Node 22).

- **1.0.0** (initial). Core surface: signal (`locale`, `_epoch`, `ready`),
  translation (`t`, `plural`), definition (`defineMessages`), async loading
  (`loadLocale`, `ready`), fallback chain (`setFallback`), missing-key
  policies (`setMissingKeyPolicy`, `onMissingKey`), instance isolation
  (`createI18n`, `setDefaultI18n`, `getDefaultI18n`), diagnostics (`stats`),
  errors (`MissingKeyError`). Format entry: four convenience formatters,
  four factory formatters, `createFormatters(i18n)` bulk binder. 76 tests
  (72 behavior + 4 zero-GC under --expose-gc), 0 failures. Retained heap
  ceilings: 100k t() calls with interpolation < 200 KB; 100k inline plural
  calls < 300 KB; 100k factory numberFormat calls < 100 KB; 1000 redefine
  cycles < 500 KB.

## When to use

- Twitch Extensions with locale-configurable UIs.
- Game HUDs, scoreboards, telemetry overlays with i18n.
- Long-running browser sessions where every KB of transient garbage matters.
- Multi-tenant SDKs where each tenant has its own locale + dict.
- SSR (one instance per request via createI18n).
- Anywhere `i18next` / `formatjs` bundle size or GC pressure is a problem.

## When NOT to use

- If you need ICU number/date skeletons INSIDE templates
  (`{n, number, ::currency/EUR}`, `{d, date, short}`) -- lite-i18n keeps
  formatting in the Format entry (`numberFormat`, `dateFormat`, etc.);
  use `@formatjs/intl-messageformat` if you must interleave format
  specs with translation text.
- If your translations require gender-marking or complex morphological
  agreement -- CLDR plural rules and `select` don't cover this.
- If you need translation-management-system integration (Crowdin, Lokalise,
  Transifex import formats) at runtime -- do the format conversion at build
  time and feed plain dicts.
- If you don't want a peer dep on lite-signal -- the reactivity is the core
  value proposition of this library.

## API summary

```ts
// Core (@zakkster/lite-i18n)

interface I18nConfig {
    locale?:              string;
    fallback?:            string | string[];
    missingKeyPolicy?:    "key" | "warn" | "throw";
    onMissingKey?:        (key: string, locale: string) => string | void;
    messages?:            Record<string, MessageDict>;
}

interface I18nStats {
    locales: number;
    keys: number;
    currentLocale: string;
    fallback: string[];
    pluralRulesCached: number;     // bounded by LOCALE_CACHE_MAX (FIFO)
    ordinalRulesCached: number;    // bounded by LOCALE_CACHE_MAX (FIFO)
    readySignalsCached: number;    // bounded by LOCALE_CACHE_MAX (fails closed)
    retiredLocales: number;        // cumulative unloadLocale removals; clear() resets
    warningsSuppressed: number;    // invalid-locale warns silenced past WARN_BUDGET (I-19)
    loadsInFlight: number;
}

interface I18n {
    readonly locale: Signal<string>;
    t(key: string, params?: MessageParams): string;
    plural(key: string, count: number, params?: MessageParams): string;
    defineMessages(locale: string, dict: MessageDict): void;
    loadLocale(locale: string, loader: () => Promise<MessageDict>): Promise<void>;
    ready(locale: string): Signal<boolean>;   // fails closed: throws LocaleCapacityError at the ceiling
    unloadLocale(locale: string): boolean;    // drop dict + rules + ready signal; true iff a dict was removed
    clear(): void;                            // reset instance to empty; keeps locale/fallback/policy
    setFallback(chain: string | string[]): void;
    setMissingKeyPolicy(p: "key" | "warn" | "throw"): void;
    onMissingKey(fn: ((key: string, locale: string) => string | void) | null): void;
    stats(): I18nStats;
}

const LOCALE_CACHE_MAX: number;           // 256 -- per-instance per-locale cache ceiling
function createI18n(config?: I18nConfig): I18n;
function setDefaultI18n(inst: I18n): void;
function getDefaultI18n(): I18n;
// BCP 47 prefix match (exact -> request truncation -> reverse prefix, case-insensitive)
function resolveLocale(requested: string, supported: string[]): string | undefined;

// Top-level helpers (default instance)
let locale: Signal<string>;               // ESM live binding
function t(key: string, params?: MessageParams): string;
function plural(key: string, count: number, params?: MessageParams): string;
function defineMessages(locale: string, dict: MessageDict): void;
function loadLocale(locale: string, loader: () => Promise<MessageDict>): Promise<void>;
function ready(locale: string): Signal<boolean>;
function unloadLocale(locale: string): boolean;
function clear(): void;
function setFallback(chain: string | string[]): void;
function setMissingKeyPolicy(p: "key" | "warn" | "throw"): void;
function onMissingKey(fn: ((key: string, locale: string) => string | void) | null): void;
function stats(): I18nStats;

class MissingKeyError extends Error {
    key: string;
    locale: string;
}

class LocaleCapacityError extends Error {  // thrown by ready() at LOCALE_CACHE_MAX
    locale: string;
    ceiling: number;
}

// Format (@zakkster/lite-i18n/format)

// Convenience (WeakMap(opts) -> Map<locale, Intl> cache; hoist opts for zero-alloc)
function formatNumber      (v: number|bigint, opts?, i18n?): string;
function formatDate        (v: Date|number,   opts?, i18n?): string;
function formatList        (items,             opts?, i18n?): string;
function formatRelativeTime(v: number, unit,   opts?, i18n?): string;

// Factory (per-locale cache local to the returned fn; unconditional zero-alloc steady state)
function numberFormat      (opts?, i18n?): (v: number|bigint) => string;
function dateFormat        (opts?, i18n?): (v: Date|number)   => string;
function listFormat        (opts?, i18n?): (items)             => string;
function relativeTimeFormat(opts?, i18n?): (v: number, unit)   => string;

function createFormatters(i18n: I18n): BoundFormatters;  // all 8 bound to instance
```

## Message template DSL

```
Template            := (Literal | Slot | ArgumentBlock | Quoted)*
Literal             := any character except '{' or "'"; # is literal here (not a slot)
Slot                := '{' Identifier '}'
ArgumentBlock       := PluralBlock | OrdinalBlock | SelectBlock
PluralBlock         := '{' Identifier ',' 'plural' ',' PluralVariant+ '}'
OrdinalBlock        := '{' Identifier ',' 'selectordinal' ',' PluralVariant+ '}'
SelectBlock         := '{' Identifier ',' 'select' ',' SelectVariant+ '}'
PluralVariant       := PluralSelector '{' SubTemplate '}'
SelectVariant       := SelectSelector '{' SubTemplate '}'
PluralSelector      := CldrSelector | '=' Digits
SelectSelector      := Identifier                 ; any bare identifier
CldrSelector        := 'zero' | 'one' | 'two' | 'few' | 'many' | 'other'
SubTemplate         := (SubLiteral | Slot | ArgumentBlock | Hash | Quoted)*
SubLiteral          := any character except '{', '#', or "'"
Hash                := '#'   ; equivalent to '{' <nearest enclosing plural/ordinal variable> '}'
Quoted              := "'" QuotedContent "'"
                       ; Only opens when the "'" is followed by '{' '}' or '#'
                       ; Inside the section, '' is a literal apostrophe.
                       ; Outside a section, '' is also a literal apostrophe.
                       ; A "'" not followed by a special char is literal.
Identifier          := [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*
```

Constraints enforced at compile time:
- Every plural / selectordinal / select block must contain an `other`
  variant. Missing -> `SyntaxError`.
- Braces must balance (respecting quoted sections). Unmatched `{` -> `SyntaxError`.
- Argument blocks (plural/select/selectordinal) nest freely inside any
  sub-template. Unsupported ICU shapes (`{n, number}`, `{d, date, short}`,
  `{n, number, ::currency/EUR}`, `{n, choice, ...}`) throw `SyntaxError`
  at define time -- same guard at any nesting depth.
- Slot keys are bare identifiers.
- Plural selectors must be one of `zero one two few many other` or `=N`. Any
  other selector (typo or unsupported ICU form) throws `SyntaxError`.

Runtime coercion:
- Nullish (`undefined` or `null`) slot values render as `""` (nullish coalesce
  on the hot path). Numeric zero and empty string render normally.
- EVERY read site uses `Object.hasOwn`, not just slots: the `{slot}`, the `#`
  inside a plural variant, the `{var, plural, ...}` / `{var, selectordinal, ...}`
  variable, the `{var, select, ...}` variable, and the plural-object `count`. So
  `{constructor}`, `{__proto__}` and any other prototype-chain identifier render
  as `""` (slot) or select the `other` variant (selector) unless supplied as an
  own property on `params`. `Object.prototype` can never decide which variant
  renders -- prior to 1.1.4 the selector reads were unguarded (I-01).
- `defineMessages` is atomic: templates compile into a staging Map first,
  committed only on success. A bad template mid-dict throws without leaving
  a partial update.
- `Intl.PluralRules` construction failure (invalid locale tag) falls back to the
  environment default and warns -- but the warning is rate-limited on a
  per-instance `WARN_BUDGET` (32), NOT per-tag (the tag set is untrusted input;
  warn-once-per-tag is a log-flood surface, I-19). Warnings past the budget are
  counted in `stats().warningsSuppressed`. The fallback rules are cached under the
  bad key, subject to the same `LOCALE_CACHE_MAX` FIFO bound as valid locales.
- `loadLocale` invokes its loader via `Promise.resolve().then(loaderFn)`, so
  synchronous throws inside the loader route through the async rejection
  path. The inflight slot clears on both success and failure -- retry works
  in every failure mode.

Plural-object entries always use `count` as the variable name (matches
TMS-export conventions and the `plural(key, count, params?)` sugar). For
custom variable names, use the inline ICU form.

Format-factory instance capture: `numberFormat(opts)`, `dateFormat(opts)`,
etc. bind the target i18n instance at factory-creation time (not per call).
If you hoist a factory at module scope and later swap the default via
`setDefaultI18n`, the factory keeps reading the original. For per-tenant or
SSR flows, pass the instance explicitly (`numberFormat(opts, tenantI18n)`)
or use `createFormatters(i18n)`. The convenience form (`formatNumber(v,
opts)`) re-resolves the default each call and does follow swaps.

## Common idioms

```js
// Reactive translation binding
import { effect } from "@zakkster/lite-signal";
import { t, locale } from "@zakkster/lite-i18n";

effect(() => (headerEl.textContent = t("header.title")));
locale.set("bg");  // headerEl updates synchronously

// Plural helper form
defineMessages("en", { items: { one: "# item", other: "# items" } });
plural("items", 3);                       // -> "3 items"

// Inline plural form
defineMessages("en", { m: "{n, plural, one {only #} other {# in total}}" });
t("m", { n: 42 });                        // -> "42 in total"

// Bound untrusted input BEFORE it reaches the caches (the I-03/I-04 fix)
import { resolveLocale, createI18n } from "@zakkster/lite-i18n";
const SUPPORTED = ["en", "de", "fr", "bg"];
const loc = resolveLocale(req.headers["accept-language"] || "", SUPPORTED) || "en";
const i = createI18n({ locale: loc, fallback: "en" });   // caches only ever see SUPPORTED

// Async chunk load with ready gate (ready() before the locale exists is the point)
import { loadLocale, ready, locale } from "@zakkster/lite-i18n";
effect(() => {
    if (!ready("bg")()) { spinner.show(); return; }
    spinner.hide();
});
loadLocale("bg", () => import("./locales/bg.js").then(m => m.default));

// Release a locale (frees the dict, both rules memos and the ready signal)
i.unloadLocale("bg");   // active/fallback unload falls through to the chain + bumps epoch
i.clear();              // reset the instance to empty (keeps locale/fallback/policy)

// Fallback chain
const i = createI18n({ locale: "de-CH", fallback: ["de", "en"] });

// Multi-tenant sandbox
const tenants = new Map();
function forTenant(id) {
    let t = tenants.get(id);
    if (!t) {
        t = createI18n({ locale: dbGetLocale(id), messages: dbGetMessages(id) });
        tenants.set(id, t);
    }
    return t;
}

// Zero-alloc formatter for a render loop
import { numberFormat } from "@zakkster/lite-i18n/format";
const scoreFmt = numberFormat({ notation: "compact" });
effect(() => scoreEl.textContent = scoreFmt(score()));
```

## Benchmark snapshot

Comparative `t()` throughput (Node 22, 1M iterations, 100k warm-up,
correctness asserted before timing; harness in `bench/`):

| Workload                        | lite-i18n    | i18next      | intl-messageformat |
| ------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------ | ------------------ |
| simple `{name}` interpolation   | 7.9 Mops/s   | 0.14 Mops/s  | 2.9 Mops/s         |
| plural (en, count=5)            | 2.3 Mops/s   | 0.18 Mops/s  | 0.37 Mops/s        |
| select (gender=male)            | 17.4 Mops/s  | 0.34 Mops/s  | 4.8 Mops/s         |
| select + plural composition     | 2.1 Mops/s   | 0.18 Mops/s  | 0.34 Mops/s        |

3-6x faster than `intl-messageformat` (formatjs), 12-56x faster than
`i18next`.

Zero-GC stress harness (Node 22, `--expose-gc`, warmed to 10k iterations
then measured):

| Workload                                                   | Retained heap |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| 1M `t()` calls with `{name}` + `{count}` interpolation    | < 1 MB        |
| 1M inline-plural calls                                    | < 1.5 MB      |
| 1M select calls (no PluralRules dispatch)                 | < 1 MB        |
| 500k select+plural composition calls                      | < 2 MB        |
| 100k `numberFormat` factory calls (currency, steady-state) | < 100 KB      |
| 1000 redefine-then-read cycles                             | < 500 KB      |
| 100k locale-switch cycles                                  | < 500 KB      |

The only unavoidable per-call allocation is the produced string.

## File layout

- `I18n.js` -- core: tokenizer, compiler, createI18n, top-level default-instance routing.
- `Format.js` -- Intl formatters, factories, createFormatters bulk binder.
- `I18n.d.ts` / `Format.d.ts` -- TypeScript declarations.
- `test/01-core.test.mjs` -- static/interpolation, nested dicts, missing-key policies, isolation.
- `test/02-plural.test.mjs` -- plural-object entries, inline ICU, exact matches, CLDR selectors across en/bg/pl/ar, selectordinal categories.
- `test/03-fallback.test.mjs` -- chain walk order, epoch bump semantics, non-fallback locale doesn't re-fire effects.
- `test/04-async.test.mjs` -- loadLocale, ready signal, in-flight dedup, error retry.
- `test/05-format.test.mjs` -- all 4 formatters, factory vs convenience, locale-switch reactivity, createFormatters.
- `test/06-zero-gc.test.mjs` -- heap retention stress (--expose-gc), 1M-iteration workloads.
- `test/07-select.test.mjs` -- select dispatch, other-fallback, composition with plural, escape handling in variants (v1.1).
- `test/08-torture.test.mjs` -- unicode edges, regex-eating templates, parser corners, numeric edges (`Infinity`/`NaN`/BigInt), prototype pollution safety, reactive reentrancy, three-axis composition (v1.1).
- `bench/run.mjs` -- comparative harness vs i18next and intl-messageformat, 4 workloads × 3 libraries × 1M iterations, correctness asserted.

## Install

```
npm install @zakkster/lite-i18n
```
